samples.summary: The hover state machine (`updateLinkHover`/`resetLinkHover`) has no test at all
samples.evidence: `updateLinkHover` is the core of this feature: it debounces via `LinkHoverDelayMS`, falls back to the cell under the pointer when no span is hit (so crossing plain text between two links does not strobe), compares by URL list so a collaborator edit refreshes the card, and must emit `null` before opening a new card when moving link-cell → link-cell. None of this is exercised. `packages/sheets/test/view/worksheet-mouse.test.ts` only adds `resetLinkHover: vi.fn()` to two hand-built contexts and asserts the mock was called — the real `resetLinkHover`/`updateLinkHover` bodies (timer clearing, callback with `null`, dedup) are never executed. A regression here ships a card stuck over the wrong cell or a strobing popover with a green suite.

samples.summary: The changed link-opening click path (read-only plain click, `e.detail === 1`, modifier for editors) is untested, and the only test that covered the old behavior was deleted
samples.evidence: `handleMouseDown` now opens a URL on a *plain* left click when `this.readOnly`, keeps Ctrl/Cmd for editors, and guards double-clicks with `e.detail === 1`. No test drives this: `grep -n mousedown packages/sheets/test` matches only `worksheet-list-popover.test.ts`, and `worksheet-readonly-editing.test.ts` covers only formula-bar/cell-input commits. Meanwhile the diff deletes `packages/sheets/src/view/__tests__/url-detect.test.ts`, which was the only coverage of the previous open-on-click detection (including its unsafe-protocol rejection at the click site). So a regression that makes an editor's ordinary click navigate away, or that opens two tabs on double-click, would pass CI.

samples.summary: New frontend popover component ships with no test, including its `isSafeUrl` href guard
samples.evidence: `SheetLinkPopover` filters `urls` through `isSafeUrl` before putting each string into an `href`, truncates via `toLabel`, and swallows clipboard rejections so the check mark is not shown on failure. There is no `SheetLinkPopover.test.tsx` anywhere (glob `packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/**/*.test.*` returns only CommentPopover, csv, image tests), even though the sibling `components/comments/CommentPopover.test.tsx` shows the harness exists. The href allowlist is a guard; if it were dropped or inverted nothing would fail. `toLabel`'s truncation branch (`tail.length > 40`) and the copy-failure branch are likewise unexercised.

samples.summary: `linksInCell` — including its dedup-by-URL rule — has no test
samples.evidence: `linksInCell(sref)` filters `renderedLinks` by sref and de-duplicates by `url` ("a cell that repeats one URL across its lines offers the reader one place to go, not three"). `packages/sheets/test/view/gridcanvas-links.test.ts` covers only `recordRenderedLink` and `linkAt`; `gridcanvas.test.ts` contains no occurrence of 'link'. The dedup and the sref filter feed the hover card's list directly, so a wrong filter shows another cell's URLs with no failing test.

samples.summary: The `MaxUrlLength` overlong-run rejection is never asserted on output
samples.evidence: `detectLinks` deliberately emits nothing when a URL run hits the 2048-char bound (`overlong ? '' : ...`), to avoid linking a truncated destination. The suite has no case asserting `detectLinks('https://example.com/' + 'a'.repeat(3000))` returns `[]` (or the intended result). The 'repeated unparseable schemes' case only times the call and asserts a ratio; it never inspects spans. A change to the bound or to the `overlong` condition (e.g. linking the truncated prefix) would go unnoticed.

samples.summary: The linearity assertion has an absolute 16 ms escape hatch that can hide superlinear growth
samples.evidence: `expect(large).toBeLessThan(Math.max(small, 2) * 8)` — when the small run is sub-millisecond (the common case for these inputs) the bound degenerates to a fixed 16 ms wall-clock budget, exactly the kind of absolute budget the comment says a ratio was chosen to avoid. A quadratic implementation whose 4x input still lands under 16 ms passes. The tests also never assert what `detectLinks` *returns* for these adversarial inputs, so a change that made the scanner fast by emitting wrong spans would still be green.

samples.summary: The new segmented text painting — and the behavior change that formula cells now get link detection — has no test
samples.evidence: `paintCell` was rewritten to draw each line in plain/link segments, to skip the per-span underline when `style?.u` is set, and to detect links on formula cells (previously `cell?.f ? null : ...`). `gridcanvas.test.ts` has zero 'link' matches and the new `gridcanvas-links.test.ts` only calls `recordRenderedLink`/`linkAt` on a hand-built `this`, so segment placement (`lineStartX + measure(prefix)`), the double-underline suppression, and the formula-cell inclusion are unexercised. Failure mode is visual (misplaced/duplicated glyphs), so it is contained, but nothing would catch it.

samples.summary: The link card placement effect (flip above, horizontal clamp, tab-switch dismissal) is untested
samples.evidence: The new `useLayoutEffect` in sheet-view computes flip-above-on-overflow and PAD clamping, and the cleanup now calls `setLinkHover(null)` on tab switch to avoid re-anchoring the card to the new tab's same-named cell. No test file covers `sheet-view.tsx` (glob of `packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/**/*.test.*` shows only csv/image/CommentPopover tests), so an off-screen or mis-anchored card would ship silently.

samples.summary: The two new assertions only verify a mock was invoked on a synthetic `this`
samples.evidence: `expect(ctx.resetLinkHover).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1)` in both existing tests asserts nothing about hover state: `resetLinkHover` is a `vi.fn()` on a hand-built context, so the real method (timer clear, `pointerOverLink = false`, callback with `null`) never runs. This is consistent with the file's existing style, but it is coverage of a call site rather than of behavior — worth pairing with a direct test of `resetLinkHover` itself.

verdict.reason: Verified independently. `updateLinkHover` (worksheet.ts:943-997) is a real state machine — 300ms debounce via LinkHoverDelayMS (:139, :993-996), cell fallback when no span is hit (:955-962), dedup by sref+URL list (:971-977), and a mandatory `null` emission before reopening on link-cell → link-cell (:983-988) — plus `resetLinkHover` (:1009-1017). Repo-wide grep for `LinkHover`/`updateLinkHover`/`resetLinkHover` finds exactly one test file, worksheet-mouse.test.ts, which only injects `resetLinkHover: vi.fn()` into hand-built contexts (lines 51, 80) and asserts the mock was called (lines 65, 92); neither real body ever executes and `updateLinkHover` is never referenced by any test. I searched wider than the original reviewer: gridcanvas-links.test.ts covers only recordRenderedLink/linkAt (painter + hit-test, lines 45-151); src/view/__tests__/cell-links.test.ts covers only detectLinks/layoutLinkBoxes/clipLinkBox; case-insensitive `hover` grep across packages/sheets yields no other candidate; frontend has SheetLinkPopover.tsx and sheet-view.tsx consumers but no test for them (no `**/*link*.test.*` match, no `hover` hit in packages/frontend/tests); no e2e directory exists. No counterexample found. Graded major: the debounce/dedup/null-emission logic drives a user-visible popover on a path users take (hovering a link cell), and a regression producing a stuck or strobing card would ship with a green suite. In-lane: a mock-call assertion presented as coverage plus no meaningful test over new behavior.

verdict.reason: The changed click-open gate is inline in the private `handleMouseDown` (packages/sheets/src/view/worksheet.ts:3678-3691: `e.button === 0 && e.detail === 1 && (this.readOnly || e.ctrlKey || e.metaKey) && isInsideGrid` then `window.open`). A repo-wide grep for `handleMouseDown|linkAtMouse|resetLinkHover`, `window.open`, and `noopener` finds no test that invokes this handler: the only sheets tests touching mouse handlers are worksheet-mouse.test.ts (handleMouseMove / handleScrollContainerMouseLeave hover clearing, lines 54-93) and gridcanvas-links.test.ts (recordRenderedLink/linkAt geometry, lines 45-151). cell-links.test.ts covers only string-level detection and safety, never the read-only/modifier/detail gate, and no extracted predicate exists to test it. There is no sheets-side url-detect test (those files exist only under packages/docs). So a regression making an editor's plain click navigate away, or opening two tabs on double-click, ships undetected — a user-visible gap with no meaningful coverage, blocking under the test-adequacy rubric.

verdict.reason: Verified the component does what the finding describes: it filters urls through isSafeUrl before rendering each string into an href (SheetLinkPopover.tsx:58 and :75), truncates labels via the tail.length > 40 branch in toLabel (:20-32), and swallows clipboard rejections so the check mark only appears on success (:88-99). I searched well beyond the reviewer's paths: repo-wide grep for SheetLinkPopover, "Links in this cell", sheet-link-popover, toLabel, and the aria-label "Copy ${...}"; plus the separate mirror test tree packages/frontend/tests/** (where the sibling docs-link-popover.test.tsx lives, proving the harness exists for exactly this kind of popover). The only non-doc references to the component are its own file and its mount at sheet-view.tsx:56/1872; packages/frontend/tests/app/spreadsheet/ has no popover test, and the only test touching sheet-view mocks it out entirely (packages/frontend/tests/app/documents/document-detail-lakehouse-tab.test.tsx:89). No e2e/Playwright tree exists. Nearest coverage is packages/core/test/url.test.ts (tests isSafeUrl itself) and packages/sheets/src/view/__tests__/cell-links.test.ts (engine-side span gating) — neither would fail if the component's own filter at line 58 were removed or inverted, and neither exercises the truncation or copy-failure branches. That is a real, unguarded gap over a security-relevant href allowlist and a user-visible copy-confirmation path; failures would be silent, so major under this lens.
